content: G.1.3. BOUNDS ON THE SECOND MOMENT ALONG THE FINITE-PARTICLE SYSTEMS
In this section, we show that along the finite-particle dynamics (16) and algorithm (20), the distributions remain in \(\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^{2dN})\).

Under Assumption 1, recall from Theorem 35 (in Section H) that there exists a unique equilibrium point \( z^{*} = (x^{*}, y^{*}) \in \mathbb{R}^{2d} \) which satisfies \( \nabla V(z^{*}) = 0 \). Define \( \mathbf{z}^{*} = (x^{*}, \ldots, x^{*}, y^{*}, \ldots, y^{*}) \in \mathbb{R}^{2dN} \). Then by construction, \( b^{\mathbf{Z}}(\mathbf{z}^{*}) = 0 \), where \( b^{\mathbf{Z}} \) is the vector field defined in (17).

Lemma 31 Assume Assumption 1. Suppose  \( Z_{t} \sim \rho_{t}^{Z} \)  evolves following the finite-particle dynamics (16) in  \( R^{2dN} \)  from  \( \mathbf{Z}_{0} \sim \rho_{0}^{Z} \in \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^{2dN}) \) . Then  \( \rho_{t}^{Z} \in \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^{2dN}) \)  for all  \( t \geq 0 \) .

Proof We note that \(\rho_t^{\mathbf{Z}}\) is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure on \(\mathbb{R}^{2dN}\) by virtue of the Brownian motion component in the dynamics (16).
